# Idempotency

Source: <https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/idempotency>

A request can time out after we have acted on it. An `Idempotency-Key` makes sending it again safe: we tie the key to the first request, and every retry with the same key returns the result of that request instead of creating another.

## Which requests need a key

| Request | Key |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/orders` | Required |
| `POST /v1/applications` | Required |
| `POST /v1/allocations` | Required |
| Every other request | Not used |

## Choose a key

- Generate one key for each order, application or allocation, such as a UUID.
- Save it with your own record before you send the request, so a crash on your side can't lose it.
- Send the same key on every retry of that request.
- Use 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, with no spaces. We compare keys byte for byte.
- Send the header exactly once. Without it you get `400 missing_required_field`, and with two you get `400 invalid_request`, each with `param` set to `Idempotency-Key`.

Keys never expire, and each key belongs to one request permanently. Your keys are separate from other partners' keys. Orders, applications and allocations also keep their keys apart, so the same key on an order and on an allocation names two different requests.

## What a retry returns

| You send | We return |
|---|---|
| A new key | The result of this request. `201` when it creates something. |
| A key you've used, with the same request | `200` and the resource as it is now. If it's now rejected, or was never sent, that error instead: the `422` with its `_rejected` code, or the `503` with its `_not_sent` code. An `unplaced` application returns `200` with its state. An allocation refused because deposits aren't enabled on the gateway returns `403 feature_not_enabled` again. We don't send anything again. |
| A key you've used, with a different request | `409 duplicate_order`, `duplicate_application` or `duplicate_allocation`. The error's `order`, `application` or `allocation` holds the `id` of the resource that owns the key. |

| Request | A retry is the same request when these match |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/orders` | `account`, `symbol`, `side`, `quantity`, `type`, `time_in_force`, `price_kobo` and `client_reference` |
| `POST /v1/allocations` | `account`, `amount_kobo` and `client_reference` |
| `POST /v1/applications` | Every field |

We compare the values after we read them, so a retry with different spacing or field order is the same request. `account` and `symbol` are compared without regard to letter case. A retry that adds, drops or changes `client_reference` is a different request.

A retry answers from what we hold for the key, even when that's a refusal. A retried order that's now `rejected` returns `422 order_rejected`, and one that was never sent returns `503 order_not_sent`, whatever the first answer was. Applications and allocations work the same way.

If the first request's outcome was not recorded, a retry returns `200` with the order, application or allocation in `sending` until it resolves. A new key for an identical order is refused with `409 similar_order_unresolved`, and for the same allocation with `409 similar_allocation_unresolved`. See [Handle an uncertain result](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/handling-uncertain).

We look up the key before we check the account or contact the broker, so a retry gets its answer even when the broker can't be reached.

## When to use a new key

Whether you can reuse a key depends on whether we stored the request.

| Response | Stored? | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `201 Created` or `200 OK` | Yes | Nothing. The key now belongs to this resource. |
| A timeout, or no response | Maybe | Send the same request with the same key. Never a new key. |
| `500 internal_error`, `503 service_unavailable` | Maybe | Send the same request with the same key. Never a new key. |
| `400 invalid_request`, `400 missing_required_field`, `400 unknown_account`, `413 request_too_large`, `415 unsupported_media_type`, `422 unknown_symbol` | No | Fix the request. You can reuse the key. |
| `401 unauthorized`, `403 insufficient_scope` | No | Nothing was done. Fix the API key or its scope, then send it again with the same `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `429 rate_limited`, `503 trading_paused` | No | Wait the `Retry-After` interval, then send it again with the same key. |
| `503 exchange_unavailable` | No | Send it again with the same key. |
| `422 limit_exceeded`, `422 wallet_too_low` | No | You can reuse the key once your limit or your wallet allows the request. |
| `409 similar_order_unresolved` | No | You can reuse the key once the earlier order resolves. See [Identical orders](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/handling-uncertain#identical-orders-while-one-is-unresolved). |
| `409 similar_allocation_unresolved` | No | You can reuse the key once the earlier allocation resolves. See [Identical allocations](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/handling-uncertain#identical-allocations-while-one-is-unresolved). |
| `502 exchange_error` | No | [Contact us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support). Sending it again does not change the result. |
| `403 feature_not_enabled` | An application: no. An allocation: yes, as refused | [Contact us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support). Sending it again does not change the result. |
| `422 allocation_rejected`, `422 application_rejected`, `422 order_rejected` | Yes, as rejected | To try again, send a corrected request with a new key. |
| `503 allocation_not_sent`, `503 application_not_sent`, `503 order_not_sent` | Yes, as never sent | Send it again with a new key. |
| `503 outcome_not_recorded` | Yes, as sending | Retrieve the resource the error's `order`, `application` or `allocation` names until it resolves. Don't send it again under a new key. |
| `409 duplicate_allocation`, `409 duplicate_application`, `409 duplicate_order` | Yes, under another request | Read the resource the error's `order`, `application` or `allocation` names before you send anything with a new key. It may be the one you intended. |

> **Warning.**
> After a timeout or a `5xx`, never retry with a new key unless the error code tells you to. A new key is a new request, and for an order that means a second order at the exchange.
